territorial_scope.description: Applies to Georgia state agencies and to contractors, subcontractors and vendors providing AI solutions or services to them.

evidence.quote: Agency - every state department, agency, board, bureau, commission, and authority

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Sets responsible-use rules for AI, generative AI, deep learning and machine learning tools used by Georgia state agencies, and duties for contractors and vendors supplying AI to the state, covering reporting, bias, accuracy, data protection, training and audit. No effective date is stated.
summary.long: This Georgia Technology Authority standard (SS-23-002) sets rules for state agencies' use of artificial intelligence, including generative AI, deep learning and machine learning tools. Agencies must use AI tools only for their intended purpose, check AI outputs for bias, inaccuracy and inappropriate content, keep records of AI tool usage, report AI tools to GTA, and designate a responsible staff member. Before procuring a new AI tool, agencies must submit a Business Solutions Review request to GTA. Service and technology contracts must require contractors and subcontractors to follow GTA policies and NIST guidance, provide their responsible AI policies, and allow agency verification. Non-agency entities must disclose testing, agree to ethical review and submit an AI development plan. Agencies must protect sensitive data used with AI, report breaches, and ensure users complete training. The State CIO or GTA OIS may order termination of use of an AI tool. Violations are subject to disciplinary action, and GTA audits AI tools found out of compliance. No effective date is stated.

notes: The document gives no date, effective date or number of its own; the number SS-23-002 appears only in the registry metadata. Section 6 refers to 'this AI Usage Policy', while the document is titled AI Responsible Use. 'GTA OIS' is used without being expanded. Section 2 contract terms restart their numbering in sub-lists. Section 1 requires agencies to report AI tools to GTA by email, while Section 2 requires a BSR form before procurement; these are separate duties, not conflicting ones. Relations to the PM and PS policies are inferred only from their listing under SCOPE and AUTHORITY.

events.note: The text gives no adoption, signature, publication, entry-into-force or application date for the Standard. Its only period is a 30-day contractual reporting term (Section 2, contract terms) that runs from contractor policy updates, not from an event of this instrument, so it was not coded as an event.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in the Standard changes legal treatment. The only numbers are a 30-day update period for contractor RAI policies (a procedural time limit, coded as an event if at all), the section and policy identifiers (SS-08-003, SS-08-045, PM-04-001, PS-08-005), and statutory citations. The Standard uses no size, value, volume or performance thresholds.
